      <title>Sinkholes, scarred land and scapegoats: the scourge of illegal gold mining in Johannesburg</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/oct/30/sinkholes-scarred-land-scapegoats-illegal-gold-mining-johannesburg</link>
      <description><p>There is no end in sight for the drivers of illegal mining, while police action appears ineffective</p><p>Cora Bailey has been encountering illegal miners ever since she first started treating injured animals in the townships around Roodepoort, west of Johannesburg, in 1991. But as the price of gold has soared, so too has activity in the abandoned mine shafts that mark the area.</p><p>In late September, dozens of <em>zama zamas</em> – the name given to illegal miners in South Africa, meaning roughly “to take a chance” in Zulu – arrived to dig for gold across the dirt road from her charity, Claw (Community Led Animal Welfare).</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/oct/30/sinkholes-scarred-land-scapegoats-illegal-gold-mining-johannesburg">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Critics cite Lana Nusseibeh’s denial of accusations the UAE is fuelling Sudan war by supporting paramilitary RSF</p><p>Members of the Sudanese diaspora and international human rights monitors have denounced the candidature of an Emirati diplomat for the top job at the UN, citing her denial of accusations that the United Arab Emirates is fuelling the war in Sudan by supporting the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces.</p><p>The UAE nominated Lana Nusseibeh last week to replace the UN secretary general, António Guterres, as he finishes his second five-year term ⁠this year, upending a race that had become gridlocked.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/30/sudanese-diaspora-human-rights-groups-denounce-uae-nominee-un-top-job">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Warnings of escalating clampdown on press freedom come after Cairo court convicts Attalah of managing an unlicensed website</p><p>Lina Attalah, a prominent Egyptian journalist and the editor-in-chief of the news outlet Mada Masr, has been released from detention by Egypt’s authorities and had her website ordered to be shut down by a court amid an intensifying crackdown on independent media in the country.</p><p>Attalah was taken briefly into custody after a Cairo court convicted her of managing an unlicensed website, prompting fresh international concerns over press freedom in Egypt.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/28/egypt-lina-attalah-mada-masr-press-freedom-clampdown">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Jean Kaseya, of the Africa CDC, warns of the illness spreading like Covid unless more funding is secured to increase preparedness and possible treatment</p><p>The “unprecedented” <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/17/what-is-ebola-why-who-says-drc-uganda-outbreak-global-health-emergency">spread of the Ebola outbreak</a> means it could reach the UK and other countries, according to one of Africa’s top health officials.</p><p>As the current outbreak reached <a href="https://www.ecdc.europa.eu/en/ebola-disease-multi-country-outbreak-2026">10,000 cases, with almost 5,000 deaths</a>, Dr Jean Kaseya, director general of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), compared the outbreak to the Covid pandemic, which first took hold in China before spreading to countries across the world, claiming millions of lives, and ravaging health systems and economies.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/oct/28/africa-ebola-outbreak-could-reach-uk-says-top-health-official">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Canada and EU announce new alliance open to like-minded countries</title>

      <description><p>Alliance for the Future, unveiled at Montreal summit and open to other countries, conceived for world ‘shaken by new storms’</p><p>Canada and Europe have announced a new alliance of like-minded nations to<strong> </strong>serve as both a “protective canopy under which our citizens can thrive” and a powerful hedge against the unpredictable nature of geopolitics, while welcoming other countries to join.</p><p>Speaking to reporters on Friday from Montreal, the prime minister, Mark Carney, and the European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, called the new partnership the Alliance for the Future and said the “deepest possible partnership between Canada and the 27-member bloc had the potential to offer unprecedented stability and opportunity”.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/30/canada-european-union-alliance">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Turkey has been hit by powerful thunderstorms and a fatal tornado this week with more heavy rain expected</p><p>Heavy rain and strong winds will continue to affect parts of south-eastern Europe and Turkey over the next few days, as an area of low pressure in the region has allowed for the formation of powerful thunderstorms. Authorities in Greece and Turkey have released severe rainfall and flooding warnings, as a further 100-150mm (nearly 4-6in) of rain is expected this week in central Greece and western parts of Turkey, with locally higher totals possible.</p><p>Travelling eastwards towards south Asia, strong winds and heavy rainfall have swept across the Indian regions of Odisha and Andhra Pradesh as Cyclone Arnab made landfall. The cyclone will weaken as it continues to traverse northwards over the coming days, though will continue to deliver heavy rain to parts of northern and central India as it does so.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/oct/30/severe-rainfall-flood-warnings-greece-turkey">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Trump beware: US voters are concerned about government corruption</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/31/trump-government-corruption-midterms-voters</link>
      <description><p>Alleged self-dealing by the president and his allies doesn’t look so good as corruption emerges as a key issue for midterm voters</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/30/government-corruption-us-midterm-poll">Government corruption a top issue for US midterm voters, exclusive poll finds</a></p></li></ul><p>Voters under 50 probably won’t remember the “<a href="https://www.nytimes.com/2019/05/17/opinion/sunday/welfare-queen-myth-reagan.html">welfare queen</a>”. But she once embodied Republicans’ claim of the underlying reason for US societal decay: the poor are a bunch of fraudsters.</p><p>Ronald Reagan introduced Linda Taylor to US voters at a rally during the Republican presidential primary season in 1976. A resident of Chicago’s South Side, Taylor had been arrested for welfare fraud. “She used 80 names, 30 addresses, five phone numbers to collect food stamps, social security, veteran’s benefits for four non-existing deceased veteran husbands,” Reagan said. “Her tax-free cash income alone has been running $150,000 a year.”</p><p>The Qatari government gifted him a <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/jan/22/boeing-jet-trump-qatari-royal-family-delivery">luxury jet</a>, potentially violating the emoluments clause of the constitution.</p><p>The UAE gained access to some tightly guarded, high-end American AI chips soon after an investment firm linked to its ruling family <a href="https://www.wsj.com/politics/policy/spy-sheikh-secret-stake-trump-crypto-tahnoon-ea4d97e8">secretly bought</a> a $500m stake in World Liberty Financial, the crypto company funded by the families of Trump and his chum Steve Witkoff.</p><p>Rich people facing criminal charges have taken <a href="https://www.forbes.com/sites/alisondurkee/2026/05/07/democrats-investigate-whether-trumps-pardons-were-pay-to-play-here-are-the-big-time-donors-and-business-allies-hes-sprung-free/">to donating to Trump’s political operations</a> and then seeking pardons or clemency. Most recently, <a href="https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/white-house/trump-pardons-former-puerto-rican-gov-wanda-vazquez-garced-rcna254457">Wanda Vázquez Garced</a>, the former governor of Puerto Rico, and the banker who paid her bribes, Julio Herrera Velutini, were pardoned after Velutini’s family gave <a href="https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/20/us/politics/julio-herrera-pardon-alina-habba.html">a $50m deal</a> to Alina Habba, Trump’s former personal lawyer, and donated $3.5m to Trump’s Maga Inc Super Pac.</p><p>The first family is also making a killing from the government. The Pentagon <a href="https://www.npr.org/2026/05/28/nx-s1-5837561/white-house-asked-pentagon-to-loan-money-to-a-company-linked-to-trumps-oldest-son">lent more than $600m </a>to Vulcan Elements, a rare earths startup, just three months after Donald Jr’s venture capital firm 1789 Capital bought a stake in the outfit.</p><p>Powerus, a drone maker <a href="https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/technology/powerus-backed-by-trump-sons-looks-to-sell-drone-interceptors-to-gulf-states-being-attacked-by-iran/articleshow/129991936.cms">backed by Eric and Donald Jr</a> is selling drone interceptors to Persian Gulf allies of the US that are under attack by Iran, enriching the kids from a misbegotten war launched by the dad without consulting Congress.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/31/trump-government-corruption-midterms-voters">Continue reading...</a></description>
